# Intro

Like CFIGRO_NONE, this uses FVS default parameters. The real difference
is in establishment: this uses a combination of Fred Hunt's observed
regeneration, and a guess at saplings to represent the 1980 influx.

CFICOP_DFLT is intended to serve as "how would someone have set
up a grow-only scenario in FVS in 1970".

# Regeneration

Ignore plot-specificc regeneration. use a spatial average over the first
survey period to see how many trees of each species establish in each
plot.

Regeneration in Quabbin is fraught. Regen was suppressed in areas from
1960 into the 1990s by excessive deer browse; hunting was re-introduced
in the 1990s to reduce the deer population.

There's very little info on regeneration / establishment, so we need
to reconstruct it. We'll use the best available info for background
rates for regeneration.

### ABP Establishment

```{r cfiabp_estab, eval = FALSE}
cfiabp_estab <- qryDWSPCFIPlotVisitTreeDetail |>
  filter(VisitTreeStatusCode == 1) |>
  left_join(
    tblDWSPCFIPlotVisitsComplete |>
      select(MasterPlotID, VisitCycle, MasterPlotVisitID),
    by = join_by(MasterPlotVisitID)
  ) |>
  left_join(
    tblDWSPCFITreesComplete |> select(MasterTreeID, SpeciesCode),
    by = join_by(MasterTreeID)
  ) |>
  inner_join(
    cfiabp_trees |>
      distinct(MasterPlotID, VisitCycle, MasterTreeID, StatusB),
    by = join_by(MasterPlotID, VisitCycle, MasterTreeID)
  ) |>
  filter(StatusB == "R")
```

## All Plots

Look at recruitment across all plots:

```{r establishment by species in all plots, eval = FALSE}
cfiabp_estab |>
  left_join(
    cfigro_plot_harvested,
    by = join_by(MasterPlotID)
  ) |>
  left_join(
    cfigro_plot_disturbed,
    by = join_by(MasterPlotID)
  ) |>
  left_join(
    species_crosswalk,
    by = join_by(SpeciesCode == SPCD)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    VisitCycle = as.character(VisitCycle),
    GENUS = if_else(GENUS == "Tree", "Other", GENUS)
  ) |>
  mutate(GENUS = fct_lump(GENUS, n = 5, other_level = "Other")) |>
  group_by(VisitCycle, GENUS, MasterPlotID) |>
  summarize(n = n(), .groups = "drop_last") |>
  summarize(n = mean(n), .groups = "drop_last") |>
  ggplot(aes(VisitCycle, n, fill = GENUS, group = GENUS)) +
  geom_col() +
  theme_bw() +
  scale_fill_manual(name = "Genus", values = eves_colors) +
  ggtitle("Quabbin CFI Recruitment in All Plots") +
  ylab("Number of Trees Recruited per Plot")
```

Some notes:

* 1970 can be discredited; plots were relocated in 1970, and this appears
  to include newly inventoried trees on relocated plots as "recruits".
* 1980 cannot be discredited; apparently there were a lot of saplings
  on the landscape in 1970, and a lot of these recruit in 1980.
* 1990 is still a bit elevated
* 2000 and after appear steady.

Recruitment is about the same in All Plots as it is in Grow-Only plots.

## Fred Hunt's Establishment Survey

Fred Hunt's 1961 Master's Thesis at UMass Amherst describes a general
rate of 254 stems of "establishment" per acre; we can use this number,
distributed according to his table 13, to set up background
establishment.

Here is Fred Hunt's Table 13 showing reproduction in
1960, from Brian Keevan, personal communication, June 12 2025.

Keevan notes:

> "Note that Hunt decided to call anything from 3 foot tall to 4.9”
> diameter ‘reproduction’."

Hunt left some species unspecified; we substitute the most common in
Quabbin for these. As an alternative, we could allocate them according
to observed species frequency.

- Red maple = red maple
- Oak = northern red oak 
- white pine = eastern white pine
- black birch = sweet birch
- white ash = white ash
- red pine = red pine
- other birch = paper birch
- other hardwoods = black cherry
- sugar maple = sugar maple
- spruce = red spruce

```{targets cficop_dflt_estab, tar_simple = TRUE}
tibble(
  Species = c(
    "White pine", "Hemlock", "Spruce", "Red Pine",
    "Sugar Maple", "Red maple", "Oak", "Black birch",
    "Other birch", "White ash", "Other hardwoods"
  ),
  Stems_Per_Acre = c(
    45, 13, 4, 10,
    8, 63, 54, 21,
    10, 16, 10
  ),
  Percent = c(
    10, 5, 2, 4,
    3, 25, 21, 8,
    4, 6, 4
  )
) |>
  mutate(
    SPCD = recode_values(
      Species,
      "Red maple" ~ 316,
      "Oak" ~ 833,
      "White pine" ~ 129,
      "Black birch" ~ 372,
      "White ash" ~ 541,
      "Hemlock" ~ 261,
      "Red Pine" ~ 125,
      "Other birch" ~ 375,
      "Other hardwoods" ~ 762,
      "Sugar Maple" ~ 318,
      "Spruce" ~ 97
    )
  ) |>
  left_join(
    species_crosswalk |> select(SPCD, FVS_SPCD),
    by = join_by(SPCD)
  ) |>
  select(SPECIES = FVS_SPCD, DENSITY = Stems_Per_Acre) |>
  mutate(STAND_CN = NA, YEAR = NA) |>
  arrange(desc(DENSITY))
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
cficop_dflt_estab |>
  rename(FVS_SPCD = SPECIES) |>
  left_join(
    species_crosswalk |>
      select(FVS_SPCD, SCIENTIFIC_NAME),
    by = join_by(FVS_SPCD)
  ) |>
  select(
    `Scientific Name` = SCIENTIFIC_NAME,
    Density = DENSITY
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Table 13. Reproduction by Species")
```

This is a point-in-time observation; there is no clear path to
converting this point-in-time observation into a recruitment
rate.

As a start, this can be put into FVS as establishment in each cycle,
which FVS will interpret as seedlings. This distribution will be refilled
each cycle, so every 10 years.

# Trees

CFI does not have seedling or sapling data. Since we lack this data
in 1970, we need to simulate the recruitment survey a landowner might
have done in order to set up the model.

We'll do this by walking established trees back through the surveys.

## Post-1970 ingrowth as 1970 Saplings

The CFI data lacks seedlings and saplings, so the 1970 inventory
is misssing a whole bunch of trees <6" DBH that establish in the
1980 inventory and later.

There are a few ways to try to deal with this:

* Put the trees in as 1980 establishment. This doesn't work for
  simulations that alter what establishment might look like in 1980.
* Put them in as saplings of estimated size in 1970. We'll do this.

There are also some 1970 saplings that establish in the 1990 inventory;
we'll try to hit those separately.

We can get estimated size by:

1. Take CFICOP_NONE treelist - FVS will have simulated growth of
   many trees, so we should be able to see them at small sizes.
2. Look at them at size of establishment: DBH > 6" and (DBH - DG) < 6"
3. (DBH - DG) was their size in the previous survey.

We can then take trees that establish in 1980, and either set their
size to mean(DBH - DG), or to DBH - mean(DG). The latter gives us
more of a distribution in size.

```{targets cficop_dflt_saplings, tar_simple = TRUE}
# Grab FVS modeled growth for recruits from CFICOP_NONE -
# this has all the plots with no harvest or disturbance.
# Note that we want all the random seeds; they'll give a more
# informative distribution of DBH and DG
tmp_dg_estab <- fvs_read_output(cficop_none, "FVS_TreeList") |>
  # Too small to be in the previous inventory
  filter((DBH - DG) < 6) |>
  # Big enough to be in this inventory
  filter(DBH >= 6) |>
  group_by(SpeciesFVS) |>
  summarise(
    DG = mean(DG * TPA), # FVS has fractional trees
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Find recruits that were saplings in 1970
cficop_dflt_saplings <- qryDWSPCFIPlotVisitTreeDetail |>
  cfi_with_visit_info(tblDWSPCFIPlotVisitsComplete) |>
  cfi_with_tree_info(tblDWSPCFITreesComplete) |>
  cfi_with_plot_info(tblDWSPCFIPlotsComplete) |>
  cfi_abp(cfiabp_trees) |>
  cfi_topocode() |>
  # Only recruits
  filter(VisitCycle >= 1980) |>
  filter(StatusB == "R") |>
  # Deal with species that FVS doesn't handle
  mutate(SpeciesCode = replace_values(
    SpeciesCode,
    320 ~ 317, # norway maple -> sugar maple
    402 ~ 403, # bitternut hickory -> pignut hickory
    740 ~ 743  # unknown aspen -> bigtooth aspen
  )) |>
  left_join(
    species_crosswalk |> select(SPCD, FVS_SPCD),
    by = join_by(SpeciesCode == SPCD)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(FVS_SPCD)) |>
  # Back-project their diameter
  left_join(
    tmp_dg_estab,
    by = join_by(FVS_SPCD == SpeciesFVS)
  ) |>
  # Some species, e.g. Red Pine ("RN") don't get DG;
  # fill in a non-crazy default (0.1"/year)
  mutate(
    DBH = conv_unit(dbhcm, "cm", "in"),
    DG = coalesce(DG, 1),
    cycles_since_1970 = (VisitCycle - 1970) / 10,
    DIAMETER = DBH - cycles_since_1970 * DG,
    # Diameter in decimal inches
    DIAMETER = floor(DIAMETER *  10) / 10
  ) |>
  filter(DIAMETER >= 1 & DIAMETER < 6) |>
  mutate(
    STAND_CN = as.character(MasterPlotVisitID),
    STAND_ID = MasterPlotID,
    TREE_CN = as.character(VisitTreeNumberDetail),
    TREE_ID = MasterTreeID,
    PLOT_ID = 1, # CFI does not use subplots, so all PLOT_IDs are 1
    INV_YEAR = 1970,
    TREE_COUNT = 1,
    HISTORY = 1, # Live tree
    SPECIES = FVS_SPCD,
    DIAMETER,
    HT = NA,
    # HTTOPK = VisitTreeTotalHeight, # Height to top kill; we don't ahve that
    # CRRATIO            WAS USED - not available
    # DAMAGE1            WAS USED - not available
    # SEVERITY1          WAS USED - not available
    # DAMAGE2            WAS USED - not available
    # SEVERITY2          WAS USED - not available
    # DAMAGE3            WAS USED - not available
    # SEVERITY3          WAS USED - not avialable
    # TREEVALUE          WAS USED - X - tree removal priority
    # PRESCRIPTION       WAS USED - X - tree removal group
    # AGE                WAS USED - X
    SLOPE = Slope,
    ASPECT = Aspect,
    # PV_CODE            WAS USED - ecoregion? - not used
    TOPOCODE = TOPOCODE, # See EssentialFVS 5.4.1.2
    # SITEPREP           WAS USED - ?
    DG = NA,
    HTG = NA
  ) |>
  select(
    STAND_CN, STAND_ID, TREE_CN, TREE_ID, PLOT_ID,
    TREE_COUNT, HISTORY, SPECIES, DIAMETER, HT,
    SLOPE, ASPECT, TOPOCODE, DG, HTG
  )
```

## Post-1970 trees as 1970 trees

There are about 350 trees whose DBH in 1980 is too big for them to 
have not recruited in 1970. This appears to be a survey error.
Translate them into 1970 trees with appropriate diameters.

Note that in 1970, minimum DBH (hardwood and softwood) was 6"; in
1980 that dropped to 5.6".

Note that roughly 50% of the 1980 recruits are big enough that they
should have been in the 1970 inventory - e.g. 14" DBH.

* This is a True Fact about the 1970 inventory - it missed ~1307 trees,
  which comes to ~5 trees per plot.
* The intent here is to simulate a sapling survey, so filter those out
* Separately, we can back-propagate the missing trees to see what
  impact they have.
  
```{targets cficop_dflt_trees_missing, tar_simple = TRUE}
# Grab FVS modeled growth for recruits from CFICOP_NONE -
# this has all the plots with no harvest or disturbance.
# Note that we want all the random seeds; they'll give a more
# informative distribution of DBH and DG
tmp_dg_estab <- fvs_read_output(cficop_none, "FVS_TreeList") |>
  # Big enough to have been in the previous inventory
  filter((DBH - DG) >= 6) |>
  # Group into 6" diameter ranges
  mutate(DBH_MIN = 6 * floor(DBH / 6)) |>
  group_by(SpeciesFVS, DBH_MIN) |>
  summarise(
    DG = mean(DG * TPA),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Find recruits that were missed in 1970
cficop_dflt_trees_missing <- qryDWSPCFIPlotVisitTreeDetail |>
  cfi_with_visit_info(tblDWSPCFIPlotVisitsComplete) |>
  cfi_with_tree_info(tblDWSPCFITreesComplete) |>
  cfi_with_plot_info(tblDWSPCFIPlotsComplete) |>
  cfi_abp(cfiabp_trees) |>
  cfi_topocode() |>
  # Only recruits
  filter(StatusB == "R") |>
  filter(VisitCycle >= 1980) |>
  # Deal with species that FVS doesn't handle
  mutate(
    SpeciesCode = replace_values(
      SpeciesCode,
      320 ~ 317, # norway maple -> sugar maple
      402 ~ 403, # bitternut hickory -> pignut hickory
      740 ~ 743  # unknown aspen -> bigtooth aspen
    ),
    DBH = conv_unit(dbhcm, "cm", "in"),
    DBH_MIN = 6 * floor(DBH / 6)
  ) |>
  left_join(
    species_crosswalk |> select(SPCD, FVS_SPCD),
    by = join_by(SpeciesCode == SPCD)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(FVS_SPCD)) |>
  # Back-project their diameter
  left_join(
    tmp_dg_estab,
    by = join_by(FVS_SPCD == SpeciesFVS, DBH_MIN)
  ) |>
  # Some species, e.g. Red Pine ("RN") don't get DG;
  # fill in a non-crazy default (0.1"/year)
  mutate(
    DG = coalesce(DG, 1),
    cycles_since_1970 = (VisitCycle - 1970) / 10,
    DIAMETER = DBH - cycles_since_1970 * DG,
    # Diameter in decimal inches
    DIAMETER = floor(DIAMETER *  10) / 10
  ) |>
  filter(DIAMETER >= 6) |>
  mutate(
    STAND_CN = as.character(MasterPlotVisitID),
    STAND_ID = MasterPlotID,
    TREE_CN = as.character(VisitTreeNumberDetail),
    TREE_ID = MasterTreeID,
    PLOT_ID = 1, # CFI does not use subplots, so all PLOT_IDs are 1
    INV_YEAR = 1970,
    TREE_COUNT = 1,
    HISTORY = 1, # Live tree
    SPECIES = FVS_SPCD,
    DIAMETER,
    HT = NA,
    # HTTOPK = VisitTreeTotalHeight, # Height to top kill; we don't ahve that
    # CRRATIO            WAS USED - not available
    # DAMAGE1            WAS USED - not available
    # SEVERITY1          WAS USED - not available
    # DAMAGE2            WAS USED - not available
    # SEVERITY2          WAS USED - not available
    # DAMAGE3            WAS USED - not available
    # SEVERITY3          WAS USED - not avialable
    # TREEVALUE          WAS USED - X - tree removal priority
    # PRESCRIPTION       WAS USED - X - tree removal group
    # AGE                WAS USED - X
    SLOPE = Slope,
    ASPECT = Aspect,
    # PV_CODE            WAS USED - ecoregion? - not used
    TOPOCODE = TOPOCODE, # See EssentialFVS 5.4.1.2
    # SITEPREP           WAS USED - ?
    DG = NA,
    HTG = NA
  ) |>
  select(
    STAND_CN, STAND_ID, TREE_CN, TREE_ID, PLOT_ID,
    TREE_COUNT, HISTORY, SPECIES, DIAMETER, HT,
    SLOPE, ASPECT, TOPOCODE, DG, HTG
  )
```


## Combined Trees

```{targets cficop_dflt_trees, tar_simple = TRUE}
cficop_dflt_trees <- cfigro_trees |>
  union_all(cficop_dflt_saplings) |>
  union_all(cficop_dflt_trees_missing) |>
  group_by(STAND_ID) |>
  # TREE_ID needs to be unique; we could try to be clever and
  # preserve MasterTreeID where possible, but it's not worth it.
  mutate(TREE_ID = row_number()) |>
  ungroup()
```

# Run FVS

This should be simple; there's no calibration.

```{targets cficop_dflt}
tar_target(
  cficop_dflt,
  {
    timestep <- 10 # years; determined by FVSne variant
    fvsbin_dir <- "~/bin" # TODO: put these in a config file
    fvs_variant <- "FVSne"      # TODO: put these in a config file
    data_dir <- "data/fvs"
    title <- "CFICOP"
    mgmt_id <- "DFLT"
    project_dir <- file.path(data_dir, paste0("FVS_", title, "_", mgmt_id))
    if (!dir.exists(project_dir)) {
      dir.create(project_dir)
    }
    
    fvs_run(
      fvsbin_dir = fvsbin_dir,
      fvs_variant = fvs_variant,
      project_dir = project_dir,
      fiadb = NULL,
      title = title,
      mgmt_id = mgmt_id,
      stands = cfigro_plot,
      trees = cficop_dflt_trees,
      regen = cficop_dflt_estab,
      num_partitions = fvs_num_partitions,
      partition = fvs_partition,
      random_seed = fvs_randseed
    )
  },
  # iteration = "vector" branches execution for each partition value (see below)
  iteration = "vector",
  # cross() and map() are unparsed targets:: functions here.
  # cross() ensures that every combination of values for its arguments is processed
  # map() distributes each value of its argument to a separate sub-target (branch)
  # so cross(randseed, map(partition)) will run each partition in a separate branch,
  # and each branch will run with each value of randseed
  pattern = cross(fvs_randseed, map(fvs_partition))
)
```

# Compare

How does default compare to NONE and SRVY?

```{r cficop_dflt_carbon_cmp, eval = FALSE}
cficop_dflt_carbon_cmp <- cficop_dflt_carbon |>
  mutate(name = "DFLT", method = "Projected") |>
  union_all(
    cficop_none_carbon |>
      mutate(name = "NONE", method = "Projected")
  ) |>
  union_all(
    cficop_srvy_carbon |>
      mutate(name = "SRVY", method = "Measured")
  ) |>
  union_all(
    cficop_none_bai |>
      select(StandID, Starting_Carbon, Projected_Carbon, Adjusted_AGLCF) |>
      group_by(StandID) |>
      summarize(
        Starting_Carbon = min(Starting_Carbon, na.rm = TRUE),
        Adjusted_AGLCF = mean(Adjusted_AGLCF, na.rm = TRUE),
        .groups = "drop"
      ) |>
      cross_join(
        tibble(Year = seq(1970, 2020, 10))
      ) |>
      mutate(
        Aboveground_Total_Live = Starting_Carbon + Adjusted_AGLCF * (Year - 1970)
      ) |>
      select(StandID, Year, Aboveground_Total_Live) |>
      mutate(name = "Best Estimate", method = "Projected")
  ) |>
  rename(
    value = Aboveground_Total_Live
  )

cficop_dflt_carbon_cmp_summary <- cficop_dflt_carbon_cmp |>
  group_by(Year, name, method) |>
  summarize(
    n = n(),
    mean = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE),
    ymin = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE) - 1.96 * sd(value) / sqrt(n),
    ymax = mean(value, na.rm = TRUE) + 1.96 * sd(value) / sqrt(n),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```
